analysis: Docs-only PR: docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md date bump (line 3) and a new table row at head line 119 describing provider-staged (non-native-bound) checkpoint import: destinations created from zeroed host bytes, eval/stream fences skipped, so staging never waits on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock; the zero source can briefly commit up to one destination outside the MLX allocator, and the import plan charges the largest as staging scratch. No source, crypto, key, identity-binding, TTL, or disk-budget behavior is changed in the supplied evidence. Relevant threats: T-041 (cache sharing/TTFT oracle, at-rest posture) and A-001. The described change is an availability/memory-accounting refinement for staging (relates to staging-reservation accounting in the T-041 detection_hint); it does not alter the at-rest artifact, HMAC lookup tags, AAD, scope folding, or authenticated-read requirements. Unverified: the actual code changes (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift) are not supplied; the patch excerpt is marked incomplete. Whether skipping eval/fences leaves restored KV state correctly ordered relative to authenticated payload copy, and whether the off-allocator commit of the zero source is charged under GlobalKVCacheBudget, cannot be confirmed here, so the next pass should inspect those source files if present in another batch. The doc itself does not weaken any documented security control, so no finding is reported.
